clue.text: Wife entered as the bell rang and smiled with her eyes  …

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so the wife's letter goes inside the ringing word

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
a small bell tinkles when it rings

explanation.surface: A wife walks in as the doorbell sounds and gives a knowing look with her eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes inside TINKLED to give TWINKLED. The ellipsis runs the sentence on into the next clue, but each clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes that sparkle with amusement or affection are said to twinkle, a smile shown in the gaze rather than the mouth.

clue.text: …  misty eyes covering a glandular infection

indicators.note: the phrase covers, or holds within it, the letters wanted, which sit across the join of its two words

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of misty into the start of eyes

explanation.surface: Watery eyes masking an inflamed gland at the edge of the eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small painful swelling on the eyelid caused by infection of an oil gland at the base of a lash.

clue.text: Chap quietly left twice for a dance

indicators.note: something that has left is no longer there, so the quiet letter departs from the word
twice tells you to write the shortened word down two times in a row

blocks.note: taken as written
p, piano, is the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A man slips quietly out of the room twice to go and dance.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAP loses its P to leave CHA, and twice gives CHA-CHA. P for quietly comes from musical notation (piano).
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha is a lively Latin American ballroom dance of Cuban origin, with a quick triple step.

clue.text: Former pupil with date in review secured

indicators.note: a review goes over material again and reorders it, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school
the fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: An old student and a scheduled date come up for review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Review' reads like a noun for an assessment, but here it is the signal to rearrange the two words before it. An old boy is a former pupil of a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to get hold of it, so secured as a past-tense verb matches it exactly.

clue.text: Funny kit shown in an illustrated tale

blocks.note: comic means funny or amusing
a team's strip is its sports kit

explanation.surface: An amusing football outfit appears in a picture book.
explanation.walkthrough: A team's strip is British for its sports kit, the shirts and shorts in club colours.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic strip tells a story in a sequence of drawn panels, so it is a story told through pictures.

clue.text: Nuisance is removed with subtlety

indicators.note: removed tells you the small word printed alongside it is taken out of the longer word

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters to be taken out

explanation.surface: An irritation is dealt with tactfully and quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'is' does double work: it reads as a verb but supplies the letters lifted out of NUISANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a fine shade of meaning or delicate distinction, which is what subtlety describes.

clue.text: Jerky motions shown in time by coven

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece sits beside the other

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
a coven is a gathering of witches

explanation.surface: A coven's dance moves are shown jerking in rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitches are sudden small involuntary spasms of a muscle, so they are jerky movements of the body.

clue.text: Clothing worn by theatregoers?

blocks.note: surface reading: smart outfits for an evening at a play
setter's reading: people who go into an operating theatre, i.e. surgeons and nurses, in their hygienic uniforms

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that theatre means the operating theatre in a hospital, not a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrubs are the loose plain garments surgical staff wear when operating, named after scrubbing up before surgery.

clue.text: "Shoe", in a manner of speaking

blocks.note: first meaning: a sturdy leather shoe with decorative perforations
second meaning: a strong regional accent, especially Irish or Scottish

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'in a manner of speaking' look like the phrase 'so to speak', but it is the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a stout perforated leather shoe and a marked regional accent, typically Irish or Scottish.

clue.text: Some plant endives for a bet

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the letters are a portion of the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of plant into the start of endives

explanation.surface: A gardener sows salad leaves in the hope of winning a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is the stake each player puts into the pot before the cards are dealt, so a wager.

clue.text: Lost Ian's carton for flowers

indicators.note: something lost is out of place, so these letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ian has mislaid the box his bouquet came in.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnations are cultivated pinks with ruffled, often scented blooms, a common cut flower for buttonholes and bouquets.

clue.text: Sadly, Kenya extremists found here in the US

indicators.note: the extremists are the outermost ends, so only the first and last letters of the country are kept

blocks.note: alas is an exclamation of sorrow
the two end letters of the country

explanation.surface: Regrettably, radicals from Kenya have turned up on American soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kenya extremists' sounds like political radicals, but it means the outside letters of Kenya.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is one of the fifty United States, so it is a place located within that country.

clue.text: First to see exotic palm wands in marshes

indicators.note: first to points at the opening letter of the next word only
exotic means strange and foreign, so these letters take an unfamiliar new arrangement

blocks.note: the opening letter of see
the fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Be the first to spot strange palm fronds growing in a wetland.
explanation.definitionFit: Swamplands are tracts of permanently waterlogged ground, which is what marshes are.

clue.text: Second-class wine sent back by rail

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so the word for the wine is read from its end

blocks.note: B is second class, after A
retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin

explanation.surface: A poor-quality wine is returned to the seller by train.
explanation.walkthrough: B is followed by RETSINA reversed, ANISTER. 'By rail' reads like train travel; rail is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A banister is the handrail running alongside a staircase, supported on its posts.

clue.text: Terribly sad about sheep in plays

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly disordered, so these letters are scrambled
about means around, so the scrambled letters surround the animal

blocks.note: the fodder for the rearrangement
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Someone is deeply upset about sheep appearing in stage shows.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters split in two to wrap around the animal, so 'about' does its work on the scrambled word, not the original.
explanation.definitionFit: Dramas are works written for performance on stage or screen, so they are plays in the theatrical sense.

clue.text: Eccentric lady contains violent riot skilfully

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, out of the normal order, so the woman's letters are rearranged
contains says the first rearranged word holds the second inside it
something violent is thrown about wildly, so the disorder's letters are also jumbled

blocks.note: the outer fodder, to be rearranged
the inner fodder, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd woman cleverly keeps a violent mob in check.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two separate rearrangements, each with its own signal, and the second sits inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means clever and dexterous with hands or mind, so adroitly is acting with skill.

clue.text: Do read novel — it's much loved

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A reader recommends a favourite book that everyone cherishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book being recommended, but it is the signal to rearrange the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to love them deeply, so adored is a past participle meaning greatly cherished.

clue.text: GP purses her lips about nothing for those who quit

blocks.note: a GP, general practitioner, is a doctor, abbreviated DR
O looks like zero, nothing
to pout is to push the lips forward

explanation.surface: A family doctor sulks at having nothing to show for patients who give up.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are written in the order DR, O, POUTS, not in clue order. A GP is a British family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropouts are people who abandon a course of study or turn away from conventional society partway through.

clue.text: Unlock to get one pup out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are let loose and put into a fresh order

blocks.note: the fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone opens the door to let one puppy out.
explanation.definitionFit: To open up a door or building is to unfasten it, so the phrasal verb matches unlocking.

clue.text: Rot talked about trick following a noise like thunder

indicators.note: following says the second word comes after the first

blocks.note: a clap of thunder is a single loud crash
a trap is a trick or ruse to catch someone out

explanation.surface: Nonsense spoken about a ruse that followed a thunderous crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the second piece first: 'following' tells you the trick is written after the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious or empty nonsense, especially the speechifying kind, so it is rubbish that is spoken.

clue.text: Operatic song with officer about a rope

indicators.note: about means around, so the officer's letters go round the song

blocks.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: An officer sings an opera solo about a length of rope.
explanation.walkthrough: Lt is the usual abbreviation for lieutenant, the junior officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a long rope with a running noose used for catching or tethering animals, a lasso.

clue.text: Vehicle carrying new top for keeper

indicators.note: new suggests the word is given a fresh form, so its letters are rearranged
a vehicle carrying something holds it inside

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
the fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A car arrives with a new roof for the zookeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeper' suggests a zoo or goal, but a captor keeps a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A captor is one who holds another person prisoner, so a keeper in the sense of a jailer.

clue.text: Accountant left to marry last year, initially showing equanimity

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letters of the words before it are used

blocks.note: CA, chartered accountant
L is the abbreviation for left
the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: An accountant left to get married last year, and took it all in their stride.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is a chartered accountant, a British professional qualification. 'Initially' covers all three of the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Equanimity is mental composure, so doing something calmly is acting in a composed, unruffled way.

clue.text: Senseless, unruly trial on air

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so these letters will not stay in order

blocks.note: the fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A chaotic court case broadcast live makes no sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Irrational means not guided by reason or logic, which is what senseless describes.

clue.text: Heads for another new opening night later

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters, so only those are taken

blocks.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Plans for yet another premiere are put off to a later date.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned word for soon or in a little while, so it means at a later time.

clue.text: Came around to reach the top

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone recovered consciousness and went on to climb to the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came around' reads as a phrase for waking up, but around is the signal to rearrange came.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point or peak of achievement, so it is the summit.

clue.text: Ovation for the Spanish composer

blocks.note: to give someone a big hand is to applaud them
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: An audience applauds a Spanish composer.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel was a German-born baroque composer working in London, famous for Messiah.

clue.text: My hot pal turned out to be a person of wide learning

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters are turned over and come out in a different order

blocks.note: the fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: My attractive friend proved to be a real brainbox.
explanation.definitionFit: A polymath is someone whose knowledge spans many different subjects, a scholar of great breadth.
